title: Cutoff-adaptive threshold-four core rule audit
question: Do the separately certified V=2, d=17, d=18 and d=19 rows admit one predeclared cutoff-adaptive threshold-four core/tail rule with every coordinate classified by a directed log-ratio interval and no threshold ambiguity?
method: Hash-pin the R-435, R-436 and R-438 finite row manifests and primary/independent run JSON authorities.
Freeze V=2, beta=8, right orientation, unconditional one-site marginal, emission ordinal zero and threshold four before classification.
For each cutoff, use the maximum midpoint row probability as reference and classify directed log-ratio intervals with strict core/tail inequalities.
Run an independent non-importing point-log control, hostile mutations and Lean finite cardinality cross-checks through the integrated verifier.
finding: The primary directed rule audit passes 31/31 and the independent control passes 33/33. All coordinates are unambiguous. The cores are d=17 [4..12], d=18 [5..12] and d=19 [5..13], with cardinalities [9,8,9]. The raw supports are not nested and the cardinalities are not monotone; no uniform tail statement is made.
decision_reason: Advance a finite rule-local audit because the adaptive classification is reproducible and independently controlled. Keep the common-core and uniform-tail gates open because the observed supports change across cutoffs.
decision_scope: Three finite V=2 rows at d=17, d=18 and d=19, beta=8, right orientation, unconditional ordinal-zero selection and threshold four.

adversarial_review.check: The row and threshold are frozen before support classification; no gap-based selection is allowed.
Every coordinate is strictly below or strictly above the threshold in the primary interval audit.
A non-importing point-log reconstruction agrees with all three finite supports.
The d=17, d=18 and d=19 supports are not silently declared nested or monotone.
No tail modulus or common-core embedding is supplied by the finite audit.
No physical, Yang--Mills or mass-gap conclusion is inferred.

assumptions: The R-435, R-436 and R-438 primary rows are directed interval authorities for the same finite selection contract.
The reference is the maximum midpoint probability within each already fixed row and is not chosen from the resulting support.
The stored endpoints have sufficient precision for strict Decimal logarithm classification.
The expected supports are finite manifest test oracles, not limit claims.
A cutoff-adaptive finite support may be non-nested and may have non-monotone cardinality.
missing_assumptions: A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform tail modulus.
Nested or transported embeddings into a common Q3 domain.
Residual-reuse closure and a common unbounded Hamiltonian core with OS/KMS/GNS identification.
A physical-sector reference and any C6 or Sector-A transfer.
boundary: R-439 is a finite cutoff-adaptive support-rule audit only. The supports are not asserted to be nested or uniform, and no common-core, physical-sector or continuum conclusion is made.
next_action: Obtain an owner-approved uniform tail estimate or full-sector completeness theorem and explicit embeddings before attempting a common-core or physical promotion.
no_overclaim: R-439 is a finite cutoff-adaptive support-rule audit only. It does not establish nestedness, uniformity, a common core, a physical sector, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang--Mills dynamics or a mass gap.
